description: Laravel applications left in debug mode (APP_DEBUG=true) expose Symfony's Ignition/Whoops debug page on any unhandled exception, which can reveal the full application .env file contents — including database credentials, mail credentials, and the APP_KEY. A leaked APP_KEY is itself directly dangerous, since Laravel uses it to sign/encrypt cookies and sessions; a known APP_KEY has previously enabled deserialization-based remote code execution.
common_risks: debug mode enabled in production, leaking .env contents on error
leaked APP_KEY enabling cookie/session forgery or deserialization RCE
exposed .env file directly reachable over HTTP
misconfigurations: APP_DEBUG=true left set in a production .env file
.env file placed inside or reachable from the public web root
default or weak APP_KEY never regenerated per deployment
attack_patterns: Trigger any unhandled exception to view the debug page and extract .env contents
Request .env directly if it's reachable under the web root
Use a leaked APP_KEY to forge a signed cookie or craft a malicious serialized payload for deserialization RCE
real_world_incidents: Leaked Laravel APP_KEYs combined with known deserialization gadget chains have been used for remote code execution against real-world Laravel applications; debug-mode .env disclosure is one of the most common Laravel misconfiguration findings in the wild.
recommended_actions: Set APP_DEBUG=false in every production environment — no exceptions.
Ensure .env is never placed inside the public web root and is excluded from version control.
Rotate APP_KEY if it's ever suspected of being exposed, which invalidates existing signed cookies/sessions.
Keep Laravel and its dependencies patched against known deserialization gadget chains.

audience_guidance.student: Laravel is a popular framework for building PHP web apps. It has a 'debug mode' meant only for local development — if it's accidentally left on in production, any error on the site can show visitors a detailed page containing your app's secret configuration, including database passwords.
audience_guidance.developer: Always set APP_DEBUG=false in production, keep .env out of the web root and out of version control, and rotate APP_KEY immediately if you suspect it leaked.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Try triggering an error (an invalid route parameter often works) to see if the debug page appears, and separately check whether /.env is directly reachable.
audience_guidance.pentester: If debug mode or a direct .env leak yields an APP_KEY, test for cookie/session forgery and known deserialization gadget chains for that Laravel version as a path to RCE.
audience_guidance.security_team: Audit production deployments for APP_DEBUG status and .env placement as a standing check, and have a rotation plan ready for any suspected APP_KEY exposure.
